title: Lettre Tate (mai 66) (Cristaux) : lettre (1966), tapuscrit (s.d.), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's May 1966 letter to Tate on crystals. On the previous page he defined p-crystals (F: M^(p) -> M), p^{-1}-structures (V), and 'bi-crystals of weight i' (FV = VF = p^i). He then passed to the isogeny category, the 'bi-isocrystals', and proposed it as the target category for a de Rham cohomology taken up to isogeny.

Example 1, end (S = Spec k, k perfect). A bi-isocrystal is a pair (E, F):
- E is a finite-dimensional vector space over K = Frac W(k);
- F is a bijective σ-semilinear map, σ being the Frobenius of W.
In modern terms this is an F-isocrystal over k. All these descriptions are compatible with tensor operations and with base change in k.

Which bi-isocrystals come from a weight-i bi-crystal, i.e. lie in the essential image of Isbicr(S,i) -> Isbicr(S)? Set V = p^i F^{-1}. The answer is: exactly those for which, for every x, the orbit of x under all noncommutative monomials in F and V is bounded. This is a 'tautology' because the W-span of such an orbit is a lattice stable under F and V.

Some i works iff the F-orbits {F^n x} are bounded. The argument: an F-stable lattice M has F^{-1}M ⊂ p^{-c}M for some c, so p^i F^{-1} M ⊂ M once i ≥ c. In slope language this says the Newton slopes are ≥ 0, and then i ≥ the maximal slope suffices.

This condition is stable under F ↦ pF, which is tensoring with the Tate object T. Grothendieck gives T 'weight 2', the motivic weight convention. It is not stable under F ↦ p^{-1}F, which is tensoring with T^{-1}. Since one wants Tate inverted, no growth condition should be imposed on the iterates of F.

Call 'effective' the bi-isocrystals coming from some Isbicr(S,i). Then every bi-isocrystal is T^{-i} ⊗ N with N effective. This is the exact analogue of passing from effective motives to motives by inverting the Lefschetz/Tate object.

Example 2 (1.13), S smooth over a perfect field k. The argument proceeds in steps:
1. The crystalline site does not essentially change if the base Spec Z is replaced by Spec W; this uses the universal property of Witt vectors (formal étaleness).
2. A crystal relative to W is a compatible system of crystals relative to W_n = W/p^{n+1}.
3. One may localize, so take S affine. Smoothness then gives compatible smooth lifts S_n over W_n.
4. On the next page: crystals on S relative to W_n are equivalent to modules on S_n with a stratification relative to W_n.
5. If S even lifts to a proper smooth X over W, EGA III formal GAGA identifies coherent crystals with coherent modules on X stratified over W. One then restricts to X_K, where coherent stratified modules are locally free with an integrable connection.
This is the standard construction later developed in Grothendieck's IHES lectures 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1966/68) and in Berthelot's thesis.
errors: 'Bi-isocristal de Tate de poids 2' is a weight convention (weight = 2 × slope, motivic normalisation), not an error. 'De façon précise' slightly overstates matters: the decomposition T^{-i} ⊗ N needs i large enough. This is implicit and correct.
The 'tautology' silently uses that a bounded W-submodule spanning E is a lattice. This is fine because W is a complete DVR and E is finite-dimensional.
Minor: W_n = W/p^{n+1}W is an indexing convention, consistent with S = S_0.

ideas.what: Essential image of weight-i bi-crystals equals bounded orbits under F and V = p^i F^{-1}; existence of some i iff F-orbits are bounded
ideas.modern_name: Effective F-isocrystals / Newton slopes in [0, i]; existence of a lattice M with p^i M ⊂ F M ⊂ M

ideas.what: Every bi-isocrystal is T^{-i} ⊗ (effective): inverting the Tate object, by analogy with effective motives
ideas.modern_name: Tate twists of F-isocrystals; effective vs. non-effective objects; F-isocrystals as a realization of motives
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (motives philosophy); Saavedra Rivano (1972) for the Tannakian formulation
ideas.where_published: Ideas present in the Grothendieck–Serre correspondence (1964) on motives; for isocrystals unsure

ideas.what: Crystals on smooth S over a perfect field via compatible smooth lifts S_n over W_n and stratified modules; base change Z -> W harmless by the universal property of W
ideas.modern_name: Crystals as modules with integrable (HPD) connection on local lifts; crystalline site over W_n
ideas.where_published: Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968)

missed.claim: Early explicit statement that the right coefficient category for p-adic de Rham cohomology up to isogeny is a rigid tensor category in which the Tate object is inverted. Effective objects are characterised by a growth/boundedness condition on Frobenius iterates. This explicitly parallels effective vs. non-effective motives. It is well-known mathematics, but documents Grothendieck's 1966 motivic motivation for F-isocrystals.
missed.quote: Comme on tient beaucoup à inverser Tate, on voit qu'il n'est pas naturel, en effet, de poser une condition de croissance sur l'ensemble des itérés de F.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: it pins down the origin of the 'Tate-inverted F-isocrystal' viewpoint, later formalized by Saavedra and Deligne, in Grothendieck's letter to Tate. It is not mathematically new.

deep.surprise_reason: The content (characterisation of effective F-isocrystals, Tate twisting, crystals via smooth lifts) is standard and was largely made public in Grothendieck's 1966–68 crystals lectures. Only the explicit motivic framing ('effective' objects, Tate of weight 2) is of mild historical interest.
transcription_corrections: The vector space is typed 'E' with an overstrike (looks like 'F' over 'E'); the reading E is correct.
'Isbicr(S,i)' in line 4 is typed over a struck-out character ('Isbicr'), the reading is right.
'Théoriquement' has overtyped letters ('Thééoriquement') in the original.
